analysis.note: Refers anaphorically to the dharmas stated first; the masculine plural is governed by the understood dharmāḥ.
The bhāṣya verse-reading retains the written visarga before chandādhimokṣa-; the vulgate's sparśādayaś is the sandhied graphic form. The difference has no syntactic or semantic consequence.

verification.detail: compound stem sparśādi as Pum/Prathama/Bahu: pass; relation bahuvrihi: unsupported (logged)

samasa.vigraha: chandāś ca adhimokṣāś ca smṛtayaś ca

analysis.note: The compound's feminine plural follows its final member smṛti; niyatāḥ below is masculine plural because it predicates the understood pañca dharmāḥ.

verification.detail: compound stem chandādhimokṣasmṛti as Stri/Prathama/Bahu: pass; relation dvandva: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: It associates the preceding triad with the instrumental dual samādhidhībhyām for purposes of enumeration, not necessarily of simultaneous occurrence.
Instrumental dual governed by saha: “with concentration and discernment.”

verification.detail: compound stem samādhidhī as Stri/Trtiya/Dvi: pass; relation dvandva: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: A declined kta-stem derived from yam with prefix ni. It predicates the five understood dharmāḥ and means restricted to a particular object, not mutual or necessary co-arising.
The first item in the ensuing enumeration of wholesome dharmas.
Marks the transition from the completed account of the viniyata dharmas to the wholesome dharmas.
Pausal hrīḥ becomes hrīr before the following vowel in apatrapā.
The third item of the wholesome enumeration.

justifications.decision: Ādyāḥ means “those stated first,” and sparśādayaḥ denotes their class; the verse therefore supplies the understood classification “universally operative” (sarvatraga), rather than the temporal adverb “today.”
options_considered: “the first [ones]”: an anaphoric reference to the dharmas already listed
“the first [ones]” without the supplied classification sarvatraga
justifications.chosen: “Those first stated—those beginning with contact—are universally operative (sarvatraga).”

evidence.quote: ādau nirdiṣṭatvād ādyāḥ sarvatragā ity arthaḥ
evidence.translation: “Ādyāḥ” means sarvatragāḥ because they were stated at the beginning.
The preceding verse had stated them first.

evidence.quote:
sparśamanaskārādayaḥ pañca dharmāḥ sarvacittam anugacchantīti sarvatragāḥ
tathā hy eta ālayavijñāne kliṣṭe manasi pravṛttivijñāneṣu cāviśeṣeṇa
pravartante
evidence.translation: The five beginning with contact accompany every mind and operate without distinction in ālayavijñāna, the afflicted manas, and the active consciousnesses.

justifications.decision: Sparśādayaḥ is an exocentric compound: “those whose beginning is contact,” not a simple coordinate phrase “contact and beginnings.”
options_considered: A coordinate expression, “contact and so forth”
A bahuvrīhi, “those for whom contact is the beginning”

evidence.translation: “Sparśādayaḥ” means those for whom sparśa is the beginning.

justifications.decision: Niyatāḥ means that the five dharmas are restricted to special, particular objects (viśeṣa), not that they are invariably present together or are simply “determined” in an unrestricted sense.
options_considered: “Fixed/determined” without specification of what is restricted

evidence.quote:
viniyatān adhikṛtyāha
chandādhimokṣasmṛtayaḥ saha
samādhidhībhyāṃ niyatāḥ
viśeṣe niyatatvād viniyatāḥ
eṣāṃ hi viśeṣa eva viṣayo na sarvaḥ
evidence.translation: The passage concerns the viniyata dharmas: they are niyata with respect to a special object, not every object.

justifications.decision: Chanda is rendered “aspiration,” adhimokṣa “resolute ascertainment,” and smṛti “mindfulness/recollection,” because Sthiramati gives their respective technical definitions.
options_considered: Chanda as a generic wish or metrical chandas
Adhimokṣa as mere approval or preference

evidence.quote:
tatra chando 'bhiprete vastuny abhilāṣaḥ
darśanaśravaṇādiprārthanā chandaḥ
sa ca vīryārambhasaṃniśrayadānakarmakaḥ
evidence.translation: Chanda is desire for an intended object, specifically wishing for seeing, hearing, and the like.

evidence.quote:
adhimokṣo niścite vastuni tathaivāvadhāraṇam
yenaivākāreṇa tan niścitam anityaduḥkhādyākāreṇa tenaivākāreṇa
tasya vastunaś cetasy abhiniveśanam
evam etan nānyathety avadhāraṇam
adhimokṣaḥ
sa cāsaṃhāryatākarmakaḥ
evidence.translation: Adhimokṣa is unwavering ascertainment of an object precisely in its ascertained aspect.

evidence.quote:
smṛtiḥ saṃstute vastuny asaṃpramoṣaś cetaso 'bhilapanatā
pūrvagṛhītasya vastunaḥ punaḥ punar ālambanākārasmaraṇam abhilapanatā
sā punar avikṣepakarmikā
cittasyālambanāntara ākārāntare vā vikṣepābhāvād avikṣepakarmikā
evidence.translation: Smṛti is non-forgetting and repeated recollective apprehension of a previously experienced object; its function is non-distraction.

justifications.decision: Samādhi is “concentration” and dhī is “discernment”; samādhidhībhyām is a dual dvandva governed by saha.
options_considered: Samādhi as merely a collective or union

evidence.quote:
samādhir upaparīkṣye vastuni cittasyaikāgratā
ekāgratā ekālambanatā
jñānasaṃniśrayadānakarmakaḥ
evidence.translation: Samādhi is one-pointedness of mind on an object to be examined, i.e. having one support.

evidence.quote:
dhīḥ prajñā
sāpy upaparīkṣya eva vastuni pravicayo yogāyogavihito 'nyathā
pravicinotīti pravicayaḥ
saṃkīrṇasvasāmānyalakṣaṇeṣv iva dharmeṣu vivekāvabodhaḥ
evidence.translation: Dhī is prajñā, discriminative examination and discerning awareness.

justifications.decision: Saha groups the preceding three and the following two into a list of five, but does not state that all five must occur together.
options_considered: Saha entails simultaneous co-occurrence of all five
Saha makes an enumerative association of the three with the two
justifications.chosen: Enumerative association only; the five may occur separately.

evidence.quote:
ete hi pañca dharmāḥ parasparaṃ vyatiricyāpi pravartante
evañ ca
yatrādhimokṣas tatra nāvaśyam itarair api bhavitavyam
evaṃ sarvatra vācyam
evidence.translation: These five operate even separately from one another; where adhimokṣa occurs, the others need not necessarily occur, and the same is to be said throughout.

justifications.decision: Atha is transitional—“then”—and śraddhā, hrī, and apatrapā begin the subsequent list of wholesome dharmas; they are not further members of the niyata group.
options_considered: Atha as a mere connective “and,” continuing the restricted group
Atha as transition to a new, wholesome list
justifications.chosen: “Then: faith, shame, and moral scruple,” beginning the wholesome list.

evidence.quote:
uktā viniyatāḥ
tadanantaroddiṣṭās tv idānīṃ kuśalā vaktavyā ity ata āha
śraddhātha hrīr apatrapā
evidence.translation: After the viniyata dharmas have been stated, the wholesome dharmas that were subsequently mentioned are now to be explained; then the verse names śraddhā, hrī, and apatrapā.

one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind reading could misanalyse ādyāḥ as connected with adya (“today”), whereas Sthiramati explicitly takes it as “those stated first” and supplies their status as sarvatraga.

It could render niyatāḥ vaguely as “determined” or infer that the five always co-occur. The commentary defines their restriction by their particular objects and expressly says that the five can operate separately.
It could attach śraddhā, hrī, and apatrapā to the preceding niyata classification. The commentary marks them instead as the opening of the wholesome (kuśala) list.
It could flatten adhimokṣa into ordinary assent and smṛti into bare memory, missing their defined functions of unshakeable ascertainment and non-forgetting, non-distraction.
analyzer_disagreements: adyāḥ: the tagger analyzes this as ad/adya. It is instead ādyāḥ, Prathama Bahu Pum of ādi, as required by Sthiramati's gloss “ādau nirdiṣṭatvād ādyāḥ” (trbh 496).
open_questions: The supplied commentary span classifies hrī and apatrapā as wholesome but does not separately define their distinct functions. Accordingly, the translation keeps their English renderings conservative rather than imposing a sharper distinction not stated in this span.
